newsitem.title: UK: UK money market suffers squeeze,seen softer Friday.
newsitem.headline: UK money market suffers squeeze,seen softer Friday.

text.p: UK money market dealers spent the Thursday on tenterhooks, first awaiting confirmation that rates would be left on hold this month, then wrestling with a one billion stg shortage which went unfunded for most of the day.
But traders said the indications were that Friday would be an easier day with a smaller shortage and softer rates.
Overnight rates ended the session in line with base rates at 5-3/4 to 5/8 percent, but they squeezed above 7.0 percent in early trade and stayed there for most of the session.
"The highest level we traded at was seven percent, but we heard about others trading at 7-1/2 percent," said a dealer at a discount house. "It has ben a very expensive day."
But he said indictions from brokers suggested an easier day on Friday.
The Bank of England dealt at unchanged rates in early operations, indicating base rates will be left unchanged until the next monetary meeting on September 23.
But the one billion stg shortage, later revised to 1.1 billion stg, went mostly unfunded for much of the day.
Only two million stg of assistance was applied for in early operations, with none at all at midday. By the end of the day only 747 million stg of bills had been purchased by the Bank.
Short sterling reacted negatively to the indication that rates were left on hold and futures sold off across the strip.
September and December both ended the day at 94.19, down seven and nine basis points respectively.

March dropped seven basis points to settle at 93.99, now fully discounting a quarter-point rate rise by the end of the first quarter, and June at 93.62 is almost factoring a further half point rate rise by mid-1997.
"Short sterling was adjusting to the view that rates will now not be cut further," said one futures trader.
In the gilt repo market, activity concentrated on the 8.0 percent gilt due 2003 and the 6.0 percent gilt due 1999 with both trading 50 basis points below General Collateral rates.
Overnight GC ended at 5-85 to 80 percent while one-week rates ended at 5-75 to 5-70 percent.
